security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code formatting, fixed documentation links, and metadata URLs. Two instructions intentionally execute local commands through an environment-derived skill root; this creates a command-execution surface if that environment is untrusted. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Runtime path is selected from AARON_SKILLS_ROOT during command execution.
remediation.suggestion: Validate that AARON_SKILLS_ROOT is an expected repository root and that scripts/registry-events.py is a trusted regular file before running it.

remediation.issue: The root-discovery command runs git as part of setup.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a host-provided, validated plugin root and fail with a clear message when it is unavailable instead of invoking git.

remediation.issue: Creator records may contain personal and contractual information.
remediation.suggestion: Keep explicit authorization and data-minimization checks, and document retention and erasure procedures for all persistent events.

content.value_statement: Creator facts can become inconsistent across campaigns, contracts, and platforms. This skill records verified roster changes through an append-only event workflow with clear provenance.
actual_capabilities: Queries current facts for a creator aggregate ID or verified handle.
Records rates, usage rights, exclusivity windows, and performance baselines with source dates.
Routes ordinary updates through pending proposals before acceptance or rejection.
Preserves event history, revisions, conflict rationale, and source provenance.
Regenerates human-readable creator views only from accepted projection state.
limitations: It does not score creator fit or recommend partners.
It does not review creator content or assign reputation labels.
Persistent changes require explicit user authorization and host capabilities.
Standalone installations can prepare proposals but cannot establish canonical registry state.

use_cases.title: Review a prior collaboration
use_cases.description: Find the latest verified rate, rights, and exclusivity facts before contacting a returning creator.

use_cases.title: Maintain campaign records
use_cases.description: Record a closed campaign rate and performance baseline with dated evidence and provenance.

use_cases.title: Resolve pending roster updates
use_cases.description: Review creator proposals in order and accept or reject each change without deleting history.

prompt_templates.title: Find a creator record
prompt_templates.prompt: What verified rate, rights, and exclusivity facts are current for creator-7f42?

prompt_templates.title: Check pending proposals
prompt_templates.prompt: Show pending creator proposals for creator-7f42 and summarize their sources and expected revisions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a campaign update
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a proposal to record the closed spring campaign rate and performance baseline for creator-7f42. Include source and date, but do not persist it.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a conflict safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the conflicting usage-rights evidence for creator-7f42. Preserve both sources and recommend an adjudication rationale without forcing a write.

output_examples.input: What did we pay creator-7f42 last time?
output: Current verified rate: USD 1,900 for the defined bundle.
One requires confirmation because its identity link is unverified.

best_practices: Use pseudonymous aggregate IDs and store only collaboration facts that are necessary.
Attach a source, date, and authorization record to every proposed change.
Confirm persistent writes and verify the projection after accepted changes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat similar names as proof that two creator profiles are the same person.
Do not manually edit the canonical event stream or delete resolved proposals.
Do not store raw contact details or credentials in event IDs or summaries.

faq.question: Can this skill recommend creators for a campaign?
faq.answer: No. Use a fit-scoring workflow for recommendations.

faq.question: Can it review published creator content?
faq.answer: No. Use a creator-content auditing workflow for content review.

faq.question: What is required before a persistent update?
faq.answer: The user must authorize the update, and the host must provide the required capability.

faq.question: How are ordinary updates handled?
faq.answer: They are stored as pending proposals and reviewed in event order.

faq.question: Can a resolved proposal be deleted?
faq.answer: No. Resolved proposals remain in the append-only event stream.

faq.question: Does it store personal contact information?
faq.answer: It instructs users to minimize personal data and avoid raw email, phone, address, and credentials.
